message.content: /unattended:brief I want a small script that tidies the contacts file ./data/contacts.csv: trim stray spaces around every field, lowercase the email column, drop rows whose email appears twice, and write the result to ./out/contacts_clean.csv. I keep runs in ./run/ and this run's folder is ./run/2026-11-12-contacts-tidy/. I only want the brief, do not start the work.

content.text:
Before I search or draft anything, three questions, each with my proposed answer:

1. What it is for. Proposal: so you can import the contacts into a mail tool without bounced duplicates.
2. What counts as the same email. Proposal: the same address after trimming spaces and lowercasing, so "Ann@x.org " and "ann@x.org" match.
3. What happens to the original. Proposal: ./data/contacts.csv is never changed; the cleaned copy goes to ./out/contacts_clean.csv and the script prints how many rows it dropped.

message.content: 1 yes. 2 yes. 3 yes, and keep the header row exactly as it is.

content.text:
Thanks, those are settled and written down in the rulings file. Last batch before I attack the brief, four things, each with my proposed answer:

1. How we will know it works. Proposal: run `python tidy.py` on the three-row test file you can check by hand; the output matches your hand-made expected file exactly.
2. If it fails. Proposal: if the script still produces a wrong row after three honest attempts, stop and report the input row and the output row; do not loosen the rule for what counts as the same email.
3. What the run may touch. Proposal: it may create and edit files only in ./out and its own run folder, and may run python and the test command; it may not delete or overwrite anything in ./data.
4. The budget cap. Proposal: a cap of 4% of this week's quota on your subscription; spend up to the cap is then the run's to make without asking you again. My estimate is 1% of this week's quota, a guess, no record, since there is no run log for a job like this yet.

message.content: 1 yes. 2 yes. 3 yes. 4 I'll set it myself: approved up to 4% of this week's quota, not more.
